chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-Amraki ibn Ali, all together, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made Hajj obligatory upon those with the capacity (al-jiddah) every year,
and this is His word, Mighty and Majestic: 'And to Allah is the pilgrimage of the House for whoever is able to undertake a journey to it.'
And whoever disbeliees, then indeed Allah is Self-sufficient of the worlds.'

He (the narrator) said, 'I said, 'So the one from us who did not perform Hajj, so he has disbelieved?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but the one who says, 'It is not like this', so he has disbelieved'.'

key_terms.لَيْسَ هَذَا هَكَذَا: It is not like this (denial of obligation)

ai.seo_question: Does not performing Hajj make a Muslim a disbeliever?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between mere omission of Hajj and actual disbelief (kufr) by linking the obligation to the Quranic condition of ability (istita'ah). It establishes that denial of the obligation itself constitutes kufr, whereas failure to perform it due to inability or neglect does not, a key nuance in Shia jurisprudence regarding the status of those who delay the pilgrimage.
